trigger: Something seems off with the fraud pipeline, can you investigate?
summary: The entire Redis cluster went down because a single node lost memory, triggering the default 'cluster-require-full-coverage=yes' setting which treats any missing slot as a total failure. This caused all dependent services (go-server and go-enricher) to stop processing transactions immediately.
reasoning: The evidence shows that when one Redis node failed, the cluster entered a CLUSTERDOWN state rather than degrading gracefully. This is due to the unmodified default configuration of 'cluster-require-full-coverage=yes', which requires all slots to be covered by at least one master. Since there are zero replicas ('--cluster-replicas 0'), losing any single node causes the entire cluster to become unavailable. The go-server and go-enricher logs confirm they stopped receiving or processing transactions exactly when this failure occurred.
